provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Honesty
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what honesty is.
The pupils should be able to identify honest actions.
Introduction:
Last term we learned about good manners.
Today we learn about honesty.
Content:
Honesty means telling the truth.
It means returning things you borrowed.
Do not take what is not yours.
Example: If you find a toy, give it to the teacher.
Class activity:
Game: Find the toy and return it to the owner.
Evaluation questions:
What is honesty?
Should you keep a toy you find?
What should you do if you borrow a book?
Summary:
Honesty is always the best choice.

topics.title: Respect for elders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to greet elders politely.
The pupils should be able to explain why we respect elders.
Introduction:
We greet our parents every morning.
Today we learn how to greet elders.
Content:
Respect means showing good manners to elders.
Greet elders with good morning or good afternoon.
Speak softly and politely to elders.
Example: When you see your teacher, say good morning ma.
Class activity:
Role play: Practice greeting different people.
Evaluation questions:
How do you greet your teacher?
Why should we respect elders?
What happens when you speak rudely?
Summary:
Respect makes elders happy.

topics.title: Patience
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wait quietly for their turn.
The pupils should be able to explain why patience is important.
Introduction:
We all want to play with the toys.
Today we learn to wait for our turn.
Content:
Patience means waiting quietly.
Good things come to those who wait.
Do not push or shout when waiting.
Example: Wait for your friend to finish drinking water.
Class activity:
Game: Pass the ball around slowly.
Evaluation questions:
What is patience?
What should you do while waiting?
Why is patience important?
Summary:
Patience helps us get good things.

topics.title: Helpfulness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to help friends who fall.
The pupils should be able to carry things for smaller children.
Introduction:
We all need help sometimes.
Today we learn to help others.
Content:
Helpfulness means helping others.
Help a friend who falls down.
Carry bags for someone smaller than you.
Example: Help your friend pick up their books.
Class activity:
Pair activity: Help each put on shoes.
Evaluation questions:
What is helpfulness?
How can you help a fallen friend?
Should you help carry heavy bags?
Summary:
Helping makes everyone happy.

topics.title: Self control
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count to ten when angry.
The pupils should be able to use words instead of hands.
Introduction:
Sometimes we feel angry.
Today we learn to control ourselves.
Content:
Self control means managing your feelings.
Count to ten when you feel angry.
Use words to solve problems, not hands.
Example: When someone takes your toy, say please give it back.
Class activity:
Game: Count to ten when music stops.
Evaluation questions:
What is self control?
What should you do when angry?
Why should we not hit others?
Summary:
Self control makes us good children.

topics.title: Gratitude
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to thank God and parents.
The pupils should be able to say thank you without being told.
Introduction:
We get many gifts from parents.
Today we learn to say thank you.
Content:
Gratitude means being thankful.
Thank God for our food and clothes.
Say thank you to everyone who helps you.
Example: Thank your mother for cooking.
Class activity:
Song: Thank you God for everything.
Evaluation questions:
What is gratitude?
Who should we thank?
What do you say when given a gift?
Summary:
Thanking makes others happy to help.

topics.title: Sharing joy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to share their sweets and toys.
The pupils should be able to explain why sharing is good.
Introduction:
We all love to play with toys.
Today we learn to share with friends.
Content:
Sharing means giving some of what you have.
Share your sweets with friends.
Share your toys with everyone.
Example: Give half of your biscuit to your friend.
Class activity:
Activity: Share colored pencils with a partner.
Evaluation questions:
What is sharing?
Why should we share?
What happens when you share?
Summary:
Sharing makes everyone happy.

topics.title: Keeping promises
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to do what they promised.
The pupils should be able to explain why keeping promises is important.
Introduction:
We make promises to our friends.
Today we learn to keep our promises.
Content:
Keeping promises means doing what you said.
If you promise to return a book, return it.
Be a child of your word.
Example: If you promise to help, help.
Class activity:
Game: Promise to do something small and do it.
Evaluation questions:
What does keeping promises mean?
What should you do if you promise to share?
Why is it bad to break promises?
Summary:
Keeping promises builds trust.

topics.title: Courage to say sorry
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to apologise when they do wrong.
The pupils should be able to explain why sorry is important.
Introduction:
Sometimes we hurt our friends.
Today we learn to say sorry.
Content:
Saying sorry means admitting mistakes.
Apologise even when it is hard.
Sorry fixes friendship.
Example: If you push someone, say I am sorry.
Class activity:
Role play: Practice saying sorry.
Evaluation questions:
When should we say sorry?
What does sorry mean?
Why does sorry fix friendship?
Summary:
Saying sorry makes friends happy again.

topics.title: Revision and drama
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act honest and kind.
The pupils should be able to talk about good behavior.
Introduction:
We learned many good things this term.
Today we practice what we learned.
Content:
We will act out honest actions.
We will show patience and kindness.
Talk about our best moment.
Example: Act returning a found toy.
Class activity:
Drama: Perform a good deed for the class.
Evaluation questions:
What did you learn this term?
Show how to be honest.
Why is being kind important?
Summary:
We are good children because we practice what we learned.
